To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the synthesis of supported Ni/Al22O3 catalyst can be more effective if NiCl2 is directly reduced by H2 during the aerosol synthesis, without the calcining step.
the reduction of NiO and the reduction of NiCl2 by hydrogen during the catalysts synthesis can be more efficient without the calcination process.
the synthesis of catalysts can be improved by eliminating the calcination step, and that the reduction temperature can be lowered by using chloride precursory for the metal.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the kinetics of NiO and chloride reduction by hydrogen and properties of Ni/Al 2O 3 and Ni-P d/Al2O 3 catalysts obtained by using oxide or chloride precursors.
the development of new methods for the synthesis of Ni- and Pd-based catalysts with improved properties.
the kinetics of NiO and nickel chloride hydrogen reduction and the synthesis of Ni-Pd/ Al2O3 catalyst by using chloride precursers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NiCl2 precursor is a promising alternative for the NiO precursor in the catalyst preparation, since the synthesis process is more efficient, and the obtained catalysts have similar properties.
NiCl2 precursor is a better choice in the synthesis of supported Ni/Al2, and Ni-Pd catalysts.

Ni/Al22O3 catalyst with chloride precursor for Ni and Ni-Pd supported catalysts with chloride precursor for Pd are more efficient and have better properties compared with catalysts with oxide precursor for Ni and Pd, respectively.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the chloride precursors are more suitable for the synthesis of the Ni and Ni-Pd catalysts, especially if the calcination step is eliminated.
the synthesis of the supported Ni/Al22O3 and supported Ni-Pd/ Al2O3 catalyst can be more effective if the calcination step is eliminated.
chloride precursor can be used for synthesis of catalysts, but only after the elimination of the calcinations step and by using the lower reduction temperature.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of NiCl2 precursor for the preparation of Ni/Al 2O3 catalyst can significantly reduce the temperature of Ni reduction.
the use of chloride precursors for Ni in the synthesis process can be beneficial in terms of reducing synthesis temperature and eliminating the calcination step.
Ni/Al2o3 catalysts with high metal dispersion and low metal content were successfully prepared without the calcination stage.
